description: Alaska's Environmentally Threatened Communities is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys. This website provides access to maps and a community dashboard to show which communities have been identified as at risk from flooding, erosion, permafrost degradation, or a combination of these geohazards; baseline data and gaps; and progress on developing forward looking community-specific risk assessments, engineering analysis, and planning tools. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal, Landslides. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Critical Facilities, Cultural and Community Services, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Transportation and Mobility, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
